name: Bloodvenom Post
summary: At Bloodvenom Post, Horde guards watch Felwood’s high cliffs above Darkshore. Their tauren-style settlement stands amid demonic taint and corrupted wildlife.

sections.title: A Precarious Foothold
sections.body: Bloodvenom Post clings to Felwood’s high cliffs above Darkshore. A narrow trail follows the corrupted southern bank of the Bloodvenom River from the main road. Traditional tauren tents, totems, and watch posts give Horde wanderers a base in the dying forest. Scouts watch demonic forces advancing through the region and study the corruption in the waters. They also track wildlife changed by the Burning Legion’s lingering power.

sections.title: Eyes Across the Ridge
sections.body: From the cliffs, Bloodvenom Post overlooks Felwood’s tainted wilds and northern Darkshore. Its remote position lets Horde forces watch night elf movements along the western coast. The camp also lies well beyond easy reach of Alliance patrols on the forest’s central road.

aliases: how to get to bloodvenom post
faq.answer: Bloodvenom Post clings to the western ridges of central Felwood. From the main north-south road, follow a narrow trail west along the rocky hillside beside the southern bank of the Bloodvenom River.
Tauren guards hold Bloodvenom Post for the Horde. Its buildings follow traditional tauren designs.

faq.q: Why is the post named Bloodvenom?
faq.answer: Bloodvenom Post takes its name from the nearby Bloodvenom River. Demonic corruption has fouled its waters and made them toxic.

faq.q: What threats do the scouts face here?
faq.answer: Scouts face Felwood’s corrupted wildlife, including rabid sabers, tainted oozes, and twisted treants. The Shadow Council and remnants of the Burning Legion also haunt the zone.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you can find shelter and a base at this camp in Felwood’s hostile wilderness. It is the Horde’s only fortified refuge in the zone.
As a tauren, you join the braves who maintain this post. You study the Legion’s damage to the land and fight the corruption harming its natural spirits.
